text: 2D perovskites on 3D perovskites. We found that the following factors contribute to affect the 2D perovskite formation: (1) Intermediate phases at the early stages of 3D perovskite crystallization which facilitate ion exchange to template the 2D perovskite growth. (2) The rigidity of 2D ligands (i.e Dion-Jacobson versus Ruddlesden-Popper) which allow an ordered 2D formation. (3) Solvent- induced (IPA) reconstruction of the 3D perovskite surface. We probed the paramter space of the above mentioned factors using grazing incidence wide angle xray scattering. 80+ samples with various conditions were screened for potential templated 2D formations at Brookhaven National Lab. We investigated several different perovskite compositions including pure FA, with 0.8%-5% MAPbBr and 0-5% Cs doping. Moreover, we looked at two types of 2D 3 ligands: hexylammonium bromide (RP) in chloroform and Hexane-1.6-diammonium bromide (DJ) in 2-propanol (IPA). The results were consistent with our hypothesis. By depositing 1.6- diammonium bromide (DJ) in 2-propanol (IPA) at early stage of the 3D perovskite formation (20 mins into annealing and 0.8% MAPbBr ), we found a new 2D perovskite phase (at 0.65 A-1) 3 formed with similar orientation distribution to that of bulk perovskites at 1 A-1. After 40 mins, a different group of 2D perovskite phases formed at (0.36, 0.72 and 1.08 A-1) where the orientation distributions are distinct from the 3D bulk. In between, a mixture of both 2D phases formed as shown in Figure 1.1. These data fulfill the requirement of Milestone 1.1.2 To further support our claim that a templated 2D perovskite formed, we doped 5% Cs into Figure 1.1 - GIWAXS measurement of 2D formations at different intermediate state during 3D annealing the perovskite composition which creates a preferred orientation in the perovskite bulk. If a templated 2D perovskite formed, the angular distribution of the 2d peaks should mimic that of the Page 12 of 54 DE-EE0009512 Massachusetts Institute of Technology perovskite bulk. In Figure 1.2, we observed the perovskite bulk became more textured. The angular distribution of the 2D perovskite peaks also changed accordingly, which indicates that a templated 2D perovskite formed. Figure 1.2 Angular distribution of the GIWAXS measurement on Cs doped 3D/2D perovskites heterostructure To understand of the mechanism of the a b c templated 2D formation, we performed in-situ grazing incidence wide angle xray scattering (in- situ GIWAXS) at synchrotron source at LBNL to identify the intermediate phases involved in the 2D perovskite formation. In additional to the data from BNL, we reproduced the templated 2D formation in a different lab with the developed protocols which fulfill the reproducibility requirement in Miletone-1B. In Figure 1.3, we show the intermediate phase evolution of the 2D perovskite on top of the 3D perovskite film during thermal annealing. The in-situ capability allows us to conclude that intially a parellel oriented intermediate phase formed at 0.36 A-1 which is gradually converted into a 2D perovskite phase at 0.65 A-1.
